body:
## What this does

Rebuilds the Join Waitlist form at `/contact` to the Stage 1 field specification in section 5 and Appendix A of *Aurixa Systems Priority Access, Qualification & Onboarding Operating Model v1.0*. Scope matches the roadmap's Week 3 exit deliverable: revised form, validation, privacy notice, confirmation page, source tracking and application ID.

### Questions and fields (section 5.2 / 5.3)

| Field | Change |
| --- | --- |
| First Name / Last Name | Renamed from "Directive First/Last Name" |
| Work Email | Renamed from "Corporate Email" |
| Mobile Number | Now **optional**; AU numbers normalise to `+61`, international numbers need a country code |
| Organisation Name | Renamed from "Entity Name" |
| Your Role | **New** required dropdown (11 options) |
| Organisation Type | Renamed from "Entity Classification"; operating-model option list |
| Approximate Annual Client or Transaction Volume | Client/transaction counts including "Not yet known", replacing the dollar brackets |
| What would you most like Aurixa to improve? | **New** required multi-select, min 1 / max 3, replacing the mandatory free-text bottleneck field |
| Anything Else We Should Know? | **New** optional 500-character note with live counter |
| Privacy Acknowledgement | **New**, required, unticked, with an inline versioned collection notice |
| Product Updates and Marketing | **New**, optional, unticked, separate from submission |

### Also in this change

- Appendix A copy deck: "Apply for Priority Access", supporting text, 60-90 second estimate, required-field note, helper text, pre-submit explanation and the "Submit Priority Access Application" button.
- Validation per section 5.4: field-specific text errors, `aria-invalid` / `aria-required`, focus moved to the first invalid control, `fieldset`/`legend` for the checkbox group, higher-contrast labels, answers preserved on error, single-column mobile layout.
- Confirmation screen (section 5.6 / A.3): application reference, masked work email, review timeframe, next-step copy and an email-correction path. The Stage 2 button appears once `VITE_READINESS_QUESTIONNAIRE_URL` is set; until then it states the secure link will be emailed.
- Non-sequential `AX-…` application ID, also sent as an `X-Application-Id` idempotency header.
- Silent UTM / referrer / landing-page capture (`src/lib/attribution.ts`).
- Intake badge is now env-controlled with an expiry that falls back to "Applications Under Review", replacing the hard-coded "Q4 Review Cycle".

## Compatibility

The existing Make.com → Airtable payload keys (`directiveFirstName`, `corporateEmail`, `entityName`, `entityClassification`, `annualOriginationTransactionVolume`, `currentTechStackBottlenecks`, …) are all still sent, so the current scenario keeps working. `currentTechStackBottlenecks` is now derived from the structured selections plus the optional note. Structured fields, consent records and attribution are added alongside.

**Needs attention before launch:** the option *values* for organisation type and annual volume have changed, so the Airtable single-select fields need the new options added. Details in `docs/waitlist-stage-1.md`.

## Testing

- `npm run lint` (tsc --noEmit) and `npm run build` pass.
- Drove the page in Chromium: empty submit produces 9 field-level text errors with the first invalid field focused; the multi-select disables further options at three; a full submission normalises input (`  Jordan ` → `Jordan`, mixed-case email lowercased, `0412 345 678` → `+61412345678`), posts the expected payload with UTM values from the landing URL, and renders the confirmation screen. Mobile (390px) renders single-column.

## Not included

Stage 2 (Business Readiness Questionnaire), the transactional email sequence, and server-side validation of the new required fields in `capture-lead` — all listed as follow-ups in `docs/waitlist-stage-1.md`.

body: ## Summary Magnus could only "see" Hevy workouts as one-line summaries in Telegram because `formatHevyWorkoutsForPrompt` stripped per-set data—even though the Hevy list API already returns full exercise/set payloads. This PR fixes the Fitness agent data pipeline so recent sessions are injected with **full set detail** (weight×reps or duration), matching the detail level already used in EOD journals. ## Root cause (RCA) | Layer | Finding | |-------|---------| | **Hevy API** | `GET /v1/workouts` returns full `exercises[].sets[]` with `weight_kg`, `reps`, `duration_seconds` — verified live | | **Bot code** | `formatHevyWorkoutsForPrompt` kept only exercise titles + set **count**, capped at 4 exercises per session | | **Cursor vs Telegram** | Cursor health agent/scripts used `hevy-latest-workout.mts` (full JSON) → rich journals; Telegram Fitness path used the summary formatter | | **Deploy / env** | Separate issue: Railway vars often missing `NOTION_*`, webhook mode, or stale Upstash — unrelated to workout parsing but caused other "bot feels broken" reports | ## Changes - **`formatHevyContext.ts`** — format every exercise with set lines (`60×10, 65×8` or `7 min`); include workout id; optional char budget (~14k) - **`hevyClient.ts`** — add `fetchHevyWorkoutById` (used by `hevy-latest-workout.mts`) - **`fitnessAgent.ts`** — system prompt notes full set detail is available - **Tests** — expanded coverage for set formatting, cardio duration, no exercise cap, truncation - **`magnus.md`** — document behaviour ## Verification ```bash npm test -- src/pillars/health/workouts/hevy/ ``` All 20 tests pass. ## Deploy note After merge, redeploy Railway so production picks up the formatter change. `HEVY_API_KEY` must remain set on the host (already required for Hevy writes).

body:
Auditoria adversarial da defesa de **BRL** (Tier 0 dinheiro). Dois consertos, ambos com **FP medido antes de instalar**.

## 1. Furo de extensão — era só `.md`

`isMemoryMarkdownPath` exigia `.endsWith('.md')`, então `.yaml`/`.json`/`.csv` sob `memory/` **passavam**. Não é teórico:

- `memory/governance/scorecards/screens/oficinaauto-serviceorders-show.yaml` tem hits **vivos hoje**
- na janela de 90 dias, **3 das 61** linhas com `R$` entraram por `.yaml`

Agora cobre `.md .mdx .yaml .yml .json .csv .txt` sob `memory/`. **Código segue fora** (`.php .jsx .py .html`) — não é conhecimento, e valor ali é fixture, não vazamento.

Extensões reais em `memory/`: `.md` 3346 · `.yaml` 239 · `.json` 33 · `.yml` 10 (nenhum `.txt`/`.csv` — entram como cobertura preventiva de custo zero).

**FP medido:** o único não-`.md` com hit na árvore é aquele scorecard, e os 2 hits dele são `R$ 0` → liberados pelo conserto 2. **FP = 0.**

## 2. Falso-positivo do `R$ 0`

`R$ 0` / `R$ 0,00` **não é valor de negócio** — é o buraco de cálculo conhecido (*"o total da OS mecânica retorna R$ 0 hoje"*). Bloquear forçava redigir um zero, apagando informação técnica.

**Medido:** 6 dos 84 tokens da árvore e 7 das 61 linhas da janela são `R$ 0` — **~11% do ruído** sai com uma regra.

Preserva o que importa — zero seguido de dígito significativo segue bloqueado, e zero na **mesma linha** que um valor real também:

```
R$ 0,50   -> bloqueia (zero seguido de significativo)
R$ 01     -> bloqueia
R$ 0      -> passa (buraco de calculo conhecido)
de R$ 0 para <valor real>  -> bloqueia (o real manda)
```

## Provas

| | |
|---|---|
| selftest | **PASS** (+11 casos: extensões alvo/não-alvo + os 4 da exceção de zero) |
| teste de registro | **PASS** (guarda contra des-registro) |
| bite-test | `.yaml`→2 · `.json`→2 · `R$ 0`→0 · `.md` real→2 · `.php`→0 |

**Caso real:** o scorecard `.yaml` agora **é alvo** e **não bloqueia** (hits são `R$ 0`). Os dois consertos se validam mutuamente.

## O que este PR NÃO resolve — e por que isso importa

O hook está armado desde **2026-07-09**, e mesmo assim **4 commits levaram ~22 linhas com `R$` para `memory/`**. A causa foi medida e **não é indisciplina**:

- **Bash escreve sem passar por hook nenhum** (heredoc, `tee`, `sed -i`, `python -c`)
- **Não existe gate de CI** sobre o conteúdo do PR — só o selftest do hook
- Dos **56 worktrees** do repo, **7 não têm `.claude/settings.json`** e **1 não tem o hook registrado** — a defesa depende do settings daquele worktree
- Escape valve `OIMPRESSO_BRL_OK`: usada **0 vezes**

Comparação que dói: multi-tenant, PII e segredo têm gate **required** no CI. Dinheiro tem **nenhum** — é o único Tier 0 cujo enforcement mora inteiro no runtime do agente local.

O gate de CI diff-only vai em PR separado (FP medido ≈ 55-60% → nasce **advisory**, ADR 0271/0275).

Applies **planning-convention 2.2.0**: adds `planning/links.py`, a Markdown link and anchor checker, and runs it as a `lint-ci` step.

Nothing else validates these files. This repo has no docs site, so every `.md` — `README.md`, `architecture/`, `planning/` — is read on GitHub, where a rotted link stays invisible until someone clicks it.

**What the apply carries** (per the convention's `APPLY.md`):
- **§1 verbatim copy** — `links.py` → `planning/links.py`, byte-identical to canonical 2.2.0.
- **§3 judgment merge** — a `check-links` recipe plus a `planning/links.py` step in `lint-ci`.
- **§2 prose** — the `## Conventions` blockquote names `just check-links`.
- `planning/.convention-version`: 2.0.0 → **2.2.0**.

Verified: `just lint-ci` clean end to end, `links: OK`.

## What it found here

- **A cross-repo link that only resolved locally.** A `../../../modern-di/docs/…` link (or equivalent) pointed outside this repo — it resolved only on a machine with the sibling repos cloned side by side, and 404s on GitHub. Repointed at the published guide. This class is exactly why the checker gained a repo-boundary check in 2.2.0.
- **`planning/decisions/` did not exist**, though the convention scaffolds it and both `architecture/README.md` and `planning/README.md` link to it. Added `.gitkeep`, matching the other integrations.

## What changed

- Replace positional locale strings with a typed `LabelNormalizationOptions`
  object across the core and addon APIs.
- Forward the same options object through collection and summary helpers.
- Add a v2.1 migration record with before-and-after examples, and keep the
  existing locale-adoption guidance consistent with the new signature.

## Why

An options object makes locale-bearing calls self-describing and provides a
stable extension point for future label-normalization controls without adding
more positional parameters.

## Impact

Consumers that pass an explicit locale must replace calls such as
`normalizeLabel(value, 'tr')` with
`normalizeLabel(value, { locale: 'tr' })`. Calls using the default `en-US`
locale keep their existing behavior and require no changes.

## Validation

- `npm run validate:release-communication`
- `npm run check` (56 tests and the packed two-package consumer smoke test)

Adds two templates for Xposure (xposureapp.net), a portfolio host for photographers:

| File | Service id | For |
| --- | --- | --- |

author: schmidt-gabriel
body:
Two settings, both off by default and both requested for the server.

## `ENCRYPTION_KEY` — encrypt file contents at rest

AES-256-GCM in 64 KiB chunks. Each file gets its own key, derived from the master with HKDF and a random per-file salt, so the nonce can be a plain chunk counter and no two files ever seal anything under the same key and nonce. Each chunk is sealed with the header, its own index, and whether it is the last one as additional data — reordering, moving a chunk between files, and cutting off the tail all fail to authenticate rather than decoding into something plausible.

**What it protects:** a stolen disk, a copied backup, another container with the volume mounted. The server holds the key, so not a compromised server, and it is not end-to-end — clients send and receive plaintext. Filenames and the tree stay in the clear; the index describes them anyway.

**Sizes and hashes never change meaning.** `size` and `sha256` always describe the plaintext, because that is what clients compare against. The scan, the watcher, the trash restore and the download path all read through the same decrypting reader, which is also seekable — so `http.ServeContent` keeps serving Range and conditional requests unchanged.

**Existing data is not stranded.** Reading copes with either form regardless of the setting, so the moment the key is set nothing breaks. `homesync key encrypt` and `homesync key decrypt` convert the tree, preserving modification times so a converted tree does not look modified and no client re-downloads anything. Both are idempotent and safe to interrupt.

### The hole the tests found

The plaintext length is derived from the file's size rather than stored. Truncating a file therefore also shrinks what we think the file is — so a reader that stops at the shorter length never reaches the damage, and cutting on a chunk boundary read back completely clean. `Open` now authenticates the final chunk before handing the file over, which is what makes sealing it as final count.

## `ADMIN_USER` / `ADMIN_NO_AUTH`

A username alongside the password, compared in constant time, with both compared every time — checking the username first would say which half was right and leak its length through the timing. Wrong either way gives one answer.

`ADMIN_NO_AUTH=true` serves the UI with no login. Useful on a network you control, and stated for what it opens: anyone reaching the port can issue device tokens, read every filename and empty the trash. A warning on startup and a banner on the page, both permanent while it is on.

## Verification

Against a container, on a real volume:

| | |
|---|---|
| Upload → bytes on disk | 54 bytes in, 94 on disk, `HSYNCE` header, no plaintext present |
| Index | reports plaintext size 54 and the plaintext SHA-256 |
| Download | byte-identical |
| `Range: bytes=4-12` | correct plaintext slice through the decrypting reader |
| Restart | `added=0 updated=0 deleted=0` — no churn, no revisions burned |
| Plaintext file on an encrypted volume | served correctly, right size and hash |
| `key encrypt` twice | `encrypted 1 file(s); 1 already in that form` → `encrypted 0; 2 already` |
| Delete → trash → restore | ciphertext in the trash, restore reports plaintext size and hash |
| `key decrypt` | back to plaintext, same size and hash as the original upload |
| Started without the key | refuses with `encrypted`, naming `ENCRYPTION_KEY` |
| Admin: wrong user, right password | rejected, same message as a wrong password |
| `ADMIN_NO_AUTH` | warning logged, `auth_required: false`, routes open |
| Neither set | routes not registered at all — 404 |

**The conformance suite passes against an encrypted server**, which is the claim that matters: the protocol is untouched and a client cannot tell.

Two out-of-band tests fail on this machine both with and without encryption — fsnotify gets no events through a macOS Docker bind mount. Verified it is the mount and not the feature: a restart indexes the file (`added=1`) and serves it correctly. CI runs on Linux, where the watcher works.

Unit tests: the chunk format (round trip across chunk boundaries, tampering, truncation, seeking, wrong key, key parsing) and the store (plaintext size and hash whichever form is on disk, mixed volumes, refusing an encrypted file with no key). `go test -race ./...` clean.

author: rjmurillo
body:
## Summary

PR #3668 unblocked 16 workflow files at the semgrep pre-push gate. The carve-out
it added is guarded by a predicate that decides whether a `shell:` value is "not
bash". Three further rounds of cross-model adversarial review, run after that PR
merged, showed the predicate is defeatable two ways. Both holes are live on
`main` today.

This PR replaces the guard's design. It does not touch the carve-out itself.

Fixes #3683
Refs #3663
Refs #3664
Refs #3684

## Type of Change

- [x] Security fix
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Specification References

| Issue | Relationship |
|---|---|
| #3683 | Fixes. The blocklist and `.exe` holes, with reproduction. |
| #3663 | Refs. The original push blocker this hardening protects. |
| #3664 | Refs. The script-injection findings the gate unmasked. |
| #3684 | Refs. The semgrep PowerShell coverage gap, out of scope here. |

No specification change.

## Changes

- Replace the name-based shell blocklist with an allowlist of inert tokens, so
  a template carrying an inline program is refused by construction.
- Shrink the tolerated interpreter set to pwsh, powershell, and python3, the
  only ones this repository declares.
- Drop the `.exe` suffix from the interpreter pattern, which let a value miss
  the runner extension table and yield an extensionless script.
- Refuse any `run:` body that opens with a shebang, since that hands
  interpreter choice to the OS and the `shell:` value stops describing it.
- Add 19 regression tests and a nine-mutation battery over the two predicates.

## Hole 1: the guard was a name-based blocklist

The shipped guard searched the remainder of a `shell:` value for a shell name.
A template reaches a POSIX shell without spelling one, so the search is
enumerable and every enumeration is incomplete. All of these passed the guard
and run `/bin/sh`:

| shape | why the name search missed it |
|---|---|
| `python3 -c "import os;os.system(...)" {0}` | `os.system` uses `/bin/sh`; no name appears |
| `python3 -c "...shell=True" {0}` | same |
| `ruby -e "system(...)" {0}` | same |
| `node -e "...String.fromCharCode(...)" {0}` | the name is built at runtime |
| ``pwsh -c "bas`h {0}"`` | a backtick escape splits the token |
| `pwsh -c "& $env:SHELL {0}"` | the name lives in an environment variable |
| `python3 -c "'bas'+'h'" {0}` | string concatenation |
| `cmd /cbash {0}` | see below |

The last one also defeats the `\b` anchor. The word boundary evaluates the whole
token `cbash`, so `bash` inside a contiguous word is invisible, and cmd accepts a
glued `/c<command>`.

`perl {0}` is not fixable from the `shell:` string at all. Per `man perlrun`, if
the script's first line starts with `#!` and lacks "perl", perl execs the
interpreter named there.

**The fix is an allowlist.** After the leading interpreter, the only tokens
permitted are flag shapes, the `{0}` placeholder, and the PowerShell call
operator. Anything able to carry an inline program is refused by construction
rather than by enumeration.

## Hole 2: `.exe` forms miss the runner extension table

The shipped pattern carried an optional `.exe` suffix so `powershell.exe` would
classify as non-bash. That convenience was the vulnerability.

The Actions runner names the temp script by looking the first token of `shell:`
up in an extension table. Read from the runner source, not inferred, the table
has exactly six keys: cmd to .cmd, pwsh to .ps1, powershell to .ps1, bash to .sh,
sh to .sh, python to .py. A miss returns the empty string, so the file gets no
extension.

| `shell:` value | file written | what runs it | safe |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pwsh -NoProfile -Command "& '{0}'"` | .ps1 | PowerShell parses it | yes |
| `pwsh.exe -NoProfile -Command "& '{0}'"` | no extension | PowerShell defers to the OS | **no** |
| `python3 {0}` | no extension | CPython compiles it, never execs | yes |

PowerShell full-parses a .ps1 before running any of it, so a trailing syntax
error kills the whole script. An extensionless file goes to the operating
system, which honours a `#!` line. A body opening `#!/bin/bash` therefore runs
under Bash despite a PowerShell `shell:` value.

Verified against pwsh 7: the shebang body ran the payload; the identical body
without the shebang failed with `Exec format error`.

**The fix removes the suffix and adds a shebang guard.** No workflow here uses an
`.exe` form, and the runner rejects a bare `pwsh.exe` with no `{0}`, so nothing
is lost.

## Why a trailing syntax error suppresses a finding

Bash executes command by command and does not full-parse first. Confirmed
directly: a script with `echo PAYLOAD_RAN` on line 2 and `if [` on line 3 prints
the payload, then errors. A body can therefore fail `bash -n`, earning the
parse-error tolerance, and still execute. The `bash -n` check from #3668 is
necessary but was not sufficient alone.

## Also: the interpreter set is now what this repository declares

Four `shell:` values are in use here: `bash` (29 uses), `pwsh` (19),
`pwsh -NoProfile -Command "& '{0}'"` (19), `python3 {0}` (2). The tolerated set
drops to pwsh, powershell, and python3. Removing cmd, node, ruby, and perl cost
zero, confirmed by the sweep below staying unchanged.

## Evidence

Gate result for every one of the 60 files in `.github/workflows`, measured on
this branch:

| | allow | finding | blocked |
|---|---|---|---|
| carve-out disabled (main's pre-#3668 behaviour) | 44 | 0 | 16 |
| this branch | 58 | 2 | 0 |

16 unblocked, 0 newly blocked, 0 still blocked. Identical to what #3668
delivered, so this hardening costs no coverage.

Nineteen attack fixtures across four trees: **0 bypasses**. That set includes a
known-answer control, and the end-to-end shebang launcher that reproduced the
live bypass. The launcher went from rc=0 (allowed, finding suppressed) to rc=2
(blocked).

Nine mutations of the two new predicates, all killed:

| mutation | tests that caught it |
|---|---|
| restore `cmd` to the interpreter set | 1 |
| restore `perl` | 2 |
| restore `node` and `ruby` | 3 |
| re-allow `/` flag shapes | 1 |
| drop the flags-only check | 8 |
| four mutations of the shebang guard | all killed |

## Tests

442 in the gate's integration suite, full suite 16872 passed and 26 skipped.
Nineteen new cases across five groups:
interpreters outside the allowlist, inline programs reaching a POSIX shell,
`.exe` suffixed forms, shebang bodies that must block, and shebangless bodies
that must still be tolerated.

## Adversarial review

Six rounds across three model families. The record is worth stating plainly
because it is the reason this PR exists:

| round | reviewer | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | my own fixtures, then the repo security agent | both concluded "no hole"; both were wrong |
| 2 | different model family, given no conclusion | found the bypass #3668 closed |
| 3 | self-attack on committed code | four more holes |
| 4 | different model family | two more |
| 5 | different model family | a real hole whose mechanism the reviewer got wrong |
| 6 | different model family | one finding, refuted empirically |

Round 5 is the instructive one. The reviewer's verdict was right and its
mechanism was wrong, and chasing the correct mechanism found a different real
hole. Verify the mechanism, not just the verdict.

Round 6's finding was that a PowerShell body invoking bash evades the gate. It
does, but not as a bypass: semgrep reports zero findings and zero errors for it,
so there is nothing to suppress. That is a ruleset coverage gap, identical on
`main`, filed as #3684.

## Residual risk

The shebang check is deliberately stricter than the kernel, which honours `#!`
only at byte 0. It also rejects a body with leading whitespace before the `#!`.
That over-blocks, costs nothing today because no workflow here opens a body that
way, and fails closed.

On a host with no Bash the carve-out cannot verify a body, so it fails closed and
those 16 files stay blocked there. That matches pre-#3668 behaviour r

## What

Declares the `action_items` composite index `(completed ASC, due_at ASC, __name__ ASC)` in `backend/database/firestore_index_registry.py`, regenerates `firestore.indexes.json` from it, and adds the regression test that would have caught its absence.

## Why

Every due-date-filtered action-item read was 500ing in prod (#10777): 55 `FailedPrecondition: 400 The query requires an index` in the 7 days to 2026-07-28, 50 of them in the last 24h. Both the chat `get_action_items` tool and `GET /v1/action-items?due_start_date=…` take the same path — `_apply_action_item_date_filters` orders a due range **ascending**, `get_action_items` adds the `completed ==` equality, and the only deployed composite was the descending twin `(completed ASC, due_at DESC)`, which does not serve that ordering.

Nothing declared any `action_items` index in the registry, so the generated manifest had no `action_items` entry at all and no gate could catch the gap.

## Failure class

`Failure-Class: new` — `FC-undeclared-serving-query-index`: a serving query's required composite index must be declared in the repository registry, not exist only as a hand-created live index. The guard artifact is the new behavioral test below, which derives the required signature from the production query builder instead of restating it.

## What I tested

- **Live reproduction against prod Firestore** (read-only, non-existent probe uid, so no user data touched) with the exact chain the issue reports — `due_at >=`/`<=`, `order_by due_at ASC`, `completed == False`:
  `400 The query requires an index. That index is currently building and cannot be used yet.` The index Firestore demands is exactly the one this PR declares; `gcloud firestore indexes composite list --project=based-hardware` shows it as `CREATING` (hand-created during the incident) and the other five `action_items` composites as `READY`.
- **New regression test drives the real read path.** `test_due_date_filtered_action_item_reads_have_a_declared_composite_index` monkeypatches `database.action_items.db` with a recorder, calls the production `get_action_items` for a due range (parametrized over `completed=None/False/True`), derives each executed equality+ordering chain's required index signature, and asserts the generated manifest declares it.
- **It fails without the fix.** Stashing only the registry + manifest change: 3 failed, with `('action_items', 'COLLECTION', (('completed','ASCENDING'), ('due_at','ASCENDING'), ('__name__','ASCENDING'))) not in declared` — the same signature Firestore's error hint names.
- `backend/tests/unit/test_firestore_query_contract.py` → **11 passed** (`.venv/bin/python -m pytest`, Python 3.11.15).
- `python3 backend/scripts/generate_firestore_indexes.py` → manifest matches the registry; `firestore_query_coverage.py --check-ratchet` and `check_firestore_model_read_boundary.py` → exit 0.
- `make preflight` with this diff → **23 checks passed** (including `firestore-index-manifest`, `firestore-query-coverage`, `failure-class-protocol`). `black --line-length 120 --skip-string-normalization` → unchanged.
- Touching the registry selects the **full backend unit suite** (774 files); ran it via `test.sh`. Everything passes except the local fast-unit CPU-time guard tripping under parallel load (CI uses the 1.0s ceiling) and `test_sync_v2.py::TestAsyncCoordinatorBehavioral::test_inline_renew_errors_cancel_before_capacity_admission_without_releasing_retry_material`, which **fails identically on `origin/main`** — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

`GET /v1/action-items` also accepts `conversation_id` alongside a due range, and those combinations (`conversation_id ASC, due_at ASC`, plus the `completed` triple) are neither declared nor deployed — same failure class, but provisioning two more composites on a hot collection is a separate call. author: lukaskaibel
body:
A superset rendered as two independent cards, so everything the *group* owns was drawn twice: the `3 of 5` socket, the note, and — the actual problem — **Add Set, duplicate and the ⋯ menu**. All three already act on the set group (`addSet(to:)` appends one set carrying both exercises' entries; the menu edits the group's type, note and exercise slots), so the second copy of each button did exactly what the first one did.

The exercises now page horizontally **inside a single card** as containerless lanes — header, metric badge, and that exercise's entry per set. The socket, the note and one unchanged action bar sit beneath them. The badge stays per lane: it scores one exercise against its own history.

### What that let us delete

- **The fork/merge rails.** `SupersetRailShape`, `supersetThreadRails`, `railZoneHeight` and `flippedVertically` existed only to split the thread across two cards and rejoin it. With one card the trunk plugs into the one socket like every other group.
- **The duplicated control bar.** Both copies collapsed into a single `controls(for:)`, now shared with the standard card too. It keeps the group's *primary* muscle colour on both lanes — the bar acts on the group, so re-tinting on swipe would imply it belongs to whichever exercise is showing.
- **The doubled note.** It was rendered on both pages, bound to the same text, only to keep their heights equal for the merge rail.

New `SupersetLaneIndicator` dots sit between the lanes and the bar; without the rails, they and the lane header are what say which exercise is up.

### One bug worth knowing about

`scrollPosition(id:)` could not drive those dots. It names the item at the scroll view's **leading edge**, and because lanes are narrower than the card, the trailing-snapped lane never has its leading edge there — the binding kept naming the neighbour peeking in that corner, so the dots sat on lane 1 forever. `anchor: .center` did not fix it. `onScrollTargetVisibilityChange(threshold: 0.6)` does, because it asks the question directly: which lane actually fills the card. It writes a separate `visibleExerciseID` that now also feeds `autopageIfNeeded`'s notion of the current lane; `pagedExerciseID` stays purely as the programmatic write channel.

### Templates

Mirrored in the same pass (AGENT.md, "Templates mirror workouts"), and their set rows drop the `Set 1` prefix for the workout side's bare `1` — the last thing making the two set rows read differently.

### Verification

- `testRecorderSupersetPager` — both lanes, dots correct

author: chznbaum
body:
## Problem

Set video/audio assets were emitted as raw HTML `<video>`/`<audio>` embeds. The most popular Standard.Site reader (Standard Reader) strips raw HTML, so those players rendered as nothing — e.g. the [Return of the Creative Web talk](https://standard-reader.app/a/did:plc:6aia7nixso6tjtnd2jnnrtqt/chazona-ecf8d6e7-8306-4943-a308-8714adb29936) showed no video. Audio embeds hit the same wall.

## Change

Replace the HTML embeds with pure Markdown that renders anywhere images and links render:

| Case | Output |
|------|--------|
| Video/audio **with** a poster | `[![alt](poster_url)](media_url)` — clickable poster frame |
| Video/audio **without** a poster | `[label](media_url)` — plain link |
| Image | `![alt](url)` (unchanged) |

The existing `poster` convention already attached a poster image to the first video **or** audio asset in a set, so this generalizes cleanly: any media with an associated poster becomes the poster-link; any media without one falls back to a plain link. The link text is the media asset's alt.

For readers that *do* support HTML, this trades the in-place native player for a poster/link — but since the dominant reader strips HTML anyway, in practice nothing is lost, and every other reader now shows something.

## Docs & tests

- `README.md` media/poster section rewritten to describe the Markdown output.
- Rewrote the video-with-poster and audio tests; added coverage for video-without-poster and audio-with-poster.
- Full suite green (97 tests, 1 pre-existing skip).

This pull request adds robust handling for private key file permissions and overwrite behavior in the `generate-certs` command. It ensures that private keys are only readable by their owner, prevents accidental overwriting of existing keys without explicit confirmation, and provides comprehensive tests for these scenarios.

**Security and overwrite handling:**
- The command now prompts the user for confirmation before overwriting an existing `private-key.pem` file, aborting the operation if declined.
- When overwriting, the old private key file is removed before writing the new one to ensure the correct (0600) permissions are set, preventing insecure permissions from persisting.
- The private key is always written with owner-only read/write permissions (`0600`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c46da7e5c80b7fc6175433145267c28fd34ade70ea177989b393ad5b84ab7eceL8-R18) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c46da7e5c80b7fc6175433145267c28fd34ade70ea177989b393ad5b84ab7eceR106-R112)

author: fudio101
body:
Second of two PRs moving Grimoire to the TanStack ecosystem. PR #78 handled dependencies; this one replaces the framework.

**Draft on purpose — CI stays red until the last commit.** The migration lands as an ordered sequence and the app does not build between the first and second step.

## Why replace the framework at all

The app is 100% server-rendered today: no client-side fetching, no API route handlers, filters carried in URL searchParams with the server re-rendering, mutations through Server Actions and `revalidatePath`.

That matters for the stated goal of "TanStack first". Staying on Next.js leaves TanStack Query and TanStack Router with nothing to do — there is no client fetching to cache and no route state to make type-safe — so only Table and Form would apply. Moving to TanStack Start is what makes the rest of the ecosystem meaningful.

The app is small enough for this to be reasonable: 5,387 lines of TS/TSX across 6 routes, with only 13 `next/*` imports. All of `src/lib/` and the 16 files in `src/components/ui/` port essentially unchanged.

## Plan

1. Scaffold the toolchain ← **done**
2. Router shell and server entry (first green build)
3. Server functions replacing Server Actions
4. Public route `/p/$code`
5. Auth and login
6. Dashboard routes
7. TanStack Form replacing react-hook-form
8. TanStack Table + Virtual
9. Hydration pass
10. Cleanup, Docker and CI

## Two findings worth flagging early

**Server functions need their own authorization.** Today `src/proxy.ts` matches `/dashboard/:path*`, and Next Server Action POSTs go to the page URL, so the matcher covers them — even though none of the four action files contains an auth check of its own. Under TanStack Start, server functions are RPC endpoints under `/_serverFn/*`, which no `/dashboard` matcher would cover, and `beforeLoad` is explicitly a UX guard rather than a security boundary. Porting the middleware alone would expose every mutation. A `requireAdmin` function middleware goes on all 13 private server functions, verified with an anonymous POST before this leaves draft.

**The public report currently over-fetches.** `/p/[code]` calls `getCategories()` for the whole category tree to build its filter options. Harmless while it stays on the server; over RPC it would ship the entire tree to anonymous visitors. It becomes a single `fetchPublicReport` returning only in-scope filter options.

## Compatibility

`src/lib/auth.ts` is untouched, so existing `session` cookies stay valid and no one is logged out. `docker-compose.yml` is unchanged — same port, env and `/app/data` volume — and existing database volumes upgrade in place.

HF-incident analysis **Issue 1** (Medium — defence-in-depth on the highest-value component; LOW disclosure).

The incident's escape was a zero-day *in the sandbox's egress proxy* — the one component mandatory to trust, directly reachable by the contained agent, and parsing attacker-influenced wire bytes. Sandy's proxy is in that same position, so its parsers should be *proven* robust, not assumed.

- **`proxy/fuzz_test.go`**: `FuzzExtractSNI` / `FuzzParseServerName` / `FuzzExtractHTTPHost` with degenerate/truncated/oversized seed corpora. Invariant: **never panic** (a panic crashes the proxy process = the agent's only egress route). 8s local fuzzing per target found no crashers (2M+ execs each).
- **THREAT_MODEL §7**: documents the proxy as an in-scope **tier-3 attack surface**, not just a control.
- **Dependabot** already covers `proxy/go.mod` (gomod, weekly) — the finding's dependency-advisory item is already in place.

**⚠️ Follow-up (workflow-scope blocked):** the CI wiring — a 30s `-fuzztime` gate per target + an advisory `govulncheck` step in the `proxy` job — is **not** in this PR because pushing `.github/workflows/` requires a `workflow`-scoped token, which this session's `gh` token lacks. body:
Fixes #1684. Split from #1533 §4.

## Problem
`.cf-page-header__menuitem` (`apps/web/src/index.css:2340`) and
`StatusMenuButton.tsx:417` both suppressed the canonical focus ring
(`outline: none` / Tailwind `outline-none`) and substituted a tint that was
**identical to their own `:hover` state** (~1.33:1 and ~1.47:1, vs. the
canonical ring's 4.7:1 at `nocturne.css:144`). A keyboard user could not tell
"this is where I am" from "this is what my mouse happens to be over" — and
the page-header overflow menu is the only path to secondary actions below
40rem.

The defect is specifically that **focus and hover are indistinguishable from
each other**, not merely that focus is faint — a fix that raises contrast on
both, or makes focus visible while leaving it identical to hover, doesn't
solve it.

## Fix
Both sites now: hover keeps its background tint; `:focus-visible` gets the
canonical accent **outline** instead (not the tint) — a categorically
different visual treatment, not a contrast-tuned variant of the same one.
Both use an **inset** (`-2px`) outline rather than the default `+2px` outset,
because both containers scroll/clip (`.cf-page-header__menu { overflow: auto
}`, the compact status-menu card) — matching the existing
`.password-input__toggle:focus-visible` / `.seg-opt:has(input:focus-visible)`
convention in `nocturne.css` (`outline-offset: -2px`) rather than inventing a
new one.

## Sibling-divergence sweep
Per the issue's request, swept every `outline: none` (CSS) and
`outline-none` (Tailwind) site in `apps/web/src`:

| Site | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `.cf-page-header__menuitem` (index.css:2340) | **Fixed** — the named site |
| `StatusMenuButton.tsx:417` | **Fixed** — the named site |
| `SessionsPage.tsx:934` (`detailHeadingRef`, `tabIndex={-1}`) | **Fixed** — a third, previously-unreported site. Focus lands here programmatically after a mobile "select a session" tap, with `focus:outline-none` and **no substitute at all**. This is the exact "pointer-driven landing, `:focus-visible` heuristic may not apply" shape `nocturne.css`'s `#login-title:focus` comment already documents and solves with an explicit `:focus` ring — this heading just hadn't followed that established convention. Fixed the same way. |
| `nocturne.css:143` `:focus { outline: none }` + `:focus-visible` on `:144` | Clean — this **is** the canonical pattern, the source of the 4.7:1 ring itself |
| `.cf-term-help__trigger:hover, :focus-visible` (index.css:428) | Clean — does **not** suppress outline, so the un-overridden canonical `:focus-visible` ring composes on top of the shared tint; ring-present vs. ring-absent keeps the states distinguishable. Verified (not assumed) by confirming no `outline: none` exists anywhere for this class. |
| `.input:hover` / `.input:focus-visible` (nocturne.css:251-252) | Clean — different `border-color` per state, outline not suppressed |
| `.cf-name-reveal` (index.css:1745, issue #632) | Not a focus-ring site — a deliberate "reveal truncated text on any of focus/hover/touch" utility, correctly identical by design |
| `Layout.tsx` account-menu items, `CharacterTrashMenu.tsx` | Clean — neither overrides outline or hover at all; rely on the untouched canonical ring |
| `NotificationsPage.tsx:598` (`focus-visible:ring-2`) | Clean — no competing hover class on that element |
| `CampaignSettingsPage.css:59` | Clean — canonical ring, not merged with hover |

## #1532
Read first per instructions. None of its listed *currently-failing* guards
(`css-tokens`, `design-system-density`, `statblock-labels`, `time-format`,
`card-hover-accent`, `encounter-aftermath`, `generate-encounter-wizard`)
cover focus-indicator distinctness, so this needed new coverage rather than
being a pre-existing regression net.

## Tests
Added `apps/web/e2e/tests/focus-hover-distinct.unit.spec.ts`
(`pw-unit.config.ts` — pure source scan, no browser/server, same style as
`design-system-density.unit.spec.ts`):
1. Pins the two named sites to genuinely different focus-vs-hover CSS/Tailwind
   declarations (not just "focus is visible").
2. Repo-wide sweep: no CSS rule merges a `:hover` selector with a
   `:focus`/`:focus-visible` selector for the same base class while also
   suppressing the outline in that same rule.
3. Repo-wide sweep: no TSX `className` merges `outline-none` with identical
   `hover:UTIL` / `focus(-visible):UTIL` Tailwind pairs.

**Fail-first proven** — stashed the three source fixes, reran:
```
✘ the two named sites keep genuinely different focus vs. hover declarations
✘ no CSS rule merges a :hover selector with a :focus/:focus-visible selector …
```

body:
Adds the findings from #17–#26 to CLAUDE.md's gotchas and verification sections, so none of it has to be rediscovered.

## The ones that cost real time

**Meraki client attribution is not trustworthy.** `recentDeviceSerial` and `recentDeviceConnection` name whichever device last *observed* a client — where APs uplink through a switch, that's the switch. 41 clients sat on one MS250 and the wired/wireless split moved between polls (4, then 9) while the dashboard showed 20+. Per-AP counts must come from `getDeviceClients`. That mistake shipped in #24 and was reverted in #25.

**The `clients` table is "active in the last 60 seconds", not "on the network"** — `getNetworkClients` is called with `timespan = interval_clients`. Still unfixed, and deliberately not a one-liner: `usage` from that endpoint is KB *over the requested timespan*, so widening it breaks the traffic deltas.

**A class-name collision made a table render as `display: grid`.** `className="grid"` hit an existing utility, so `table-layout` and the colgroup were inert and header columns drifted from body columns. Invisible in the stylesheet, obvious in `getComputedStyle`.

**React state is async** — reading the DOM in the same call as the click that changed it returns the pre-render state and produces confident nonsense.

**The browser pane reports `document.hidden` and doesn't advance CSS animations**, so anything gated on visibility looks broken when it isn't.

## Also recorded

- Measured Meraki field population: `hostname` **0** of 68, `description` 59, `manufacturer` 60, `os` 35, `vlan` **0** — names come from `description`, and there's no VLAN column because there'd be nothing in it.
- FTD field names can contain spaces (`Prefilter Policy`), which is what #21 fixed.
- Access control policy blocks arrive as connection events (`430002`/`430003`), not `106023` — and Security Intelligence rides on the same IDs with no dedicated message ID.
- `resolve_networks` caches for the process lifetime, so a brand-new Meraki *network* needs a collector restart.

## Roadmap

Now states that the original seven-phase plan is finished and everything since is new scope, and explains **why Endpoints is NetFlow-first** — so the inversion doesn't get undone by someone assuming Meraki should be the source of truth.

Documentation only.

author: gsmecher
body:
On-line compression (that is, concurrent, reader-visible updates to a compressed dirfile) is a useful and unserved operating point for getdata: network bandwidth is cheap, the SSDs needed to sustain these rates aren't bottomless, and clients like kst rely on low-latency refresh. However, current compression plug-ins are "out-of-place", meaning data isn't visible to readers until the writer has flushed or closed the dirfile -- this doesn't help for interactive uses.

Zstd is an in-place plug-in that compresses in configurable blocks and maintains the existing "read-while-writing" behaviour that RAW fields give. Zstd has a few technical attributes (decompressed size in frame header at the beginning of the frame; skippable metadata frames; frame scans without decompression; checksums) that make it particularly well-suited to this scheme.

The main design quirk in this implementation is the maintenance of an in-memory "seek table" that's built up with a linear frame scan when a file is opened. This frame scan takes ~seconds on multi-GB compressed fields but does grow linearly. It could be improved in a future revision with a journal-type scheme. Another alternative is a "chunking" scheme at the getdata (not encoding) layer that spreads fields across multiple files; this would address similar limitations for other plug-ins as well. Both of these approaches are out-of-scope for now.

Also included are

author: alefcastelo
body:
Closes #14 (slice 3 of 13 from #11).

⚠️ **Stacked on #26** (issue #13) — base is `fix/counterpart-removed-properties`, not `main`. Both PRs edit the same two laterals; merge #26 first and this retargets to `main` cleanly.

## Problem

Counterpart resolution anchored on `(SELECT MAX(id) FROM contracts WHERE participant_id = r.participant_id)` — the counterpart's latest *published* contract. `can-i-deploy` is supposed to answer "am I compatible with what is running in this environment", so a provider that has published v5 while only v3 is deployed produced a verdict computed against v5.

The deployed version was already resolved correctly for `participantVersion` on the wire, so the response named v3 while comparing v5's schema.

## Change

Both counterpart queries gain an `anchor` LATERAL resolving the contract behind the version deployed in the target environment, with `COALESCE` back to `MAX(id)` when the counterpart has no deployment there — that fallback only ever feeds the `provider_resource_not_deployed_in_environment` break, never a property comparison. Both the `resource_versions` and `property_versions` laterals are then bounded by `anchor.contract_id`.

`GetProviderResourceByConsumerResource` takes an `environmentID` so its query can resolve `$3`; `checkConsumer` passes `environment.ID`. The consumes-side query already had the environment and reuses its existing `dep` lateral.

The anchor resolves through `contracts.version` at this stage; #20 re-points it at `contract_versions` once aliases exist.

## Tests

Both directions, each publishing an incompatible version that is never deployed:

- `TestCanIDeploy_ChecksProviderAtItsDeployedVersion` — `api` v1 (`$.id` string) deployed, v2 (`$.id` integer) published only; consumer `front` v1 stays green.
- `TestCanIDeploy_ChecksConsumerAtItsDeployedVersion` — `front` v1 deployed, v2 (`$.id` integer + required `$.name`) published only; provider `api` v1 stays green.

Both assert `participantVersion == "v1"`, so the version reported is provably the version compared. Verified to fail on the pre-fix SQL with the undeployed v2's schema leaking in:

```
Should be empty, but was map[/things:map[get:map[200:[
  {property_missing_in_provider map[property:$.name ...]}
  {property_type_mismatch map[consumerPropertyType:integer property:$.id providerPropertyType:string ...]}]]]]
```

## Acceptance

- [x] Provider deployed at v1, later publishes an incompatible v2 — verdict stays green
- [x] Same in reverse for the provides side
- [x] `go test ./...` green

body:
Compared Gaussian, Gamma and Tweedie families on the same joint specification (fixed formula and data).

### Diagnostics

Using a Tweedie family created a large improvement. The Tweedie power parameter is estimated at 1.99 (the upper limit of `mgcv`), so the fitted family is effectively Gamma.

Comparison:

Family | AIC | Deviance explained | Residual skew | Residual kurtosis | Converged
-- | -- | -- | -- | -- | --
gaussian(log) | 262,977 | 0.286 | 5.84 | 77.5 | yes
Gamma(log) | −104,260 | 0.378 | 0.52 | 9.4 | no
tw(log), p=1.99 | −103,072 | 0.380 | 0.58 | 9.2 | yes

Also investigated whether the skew was a data artefact.

- Checked the impact of the `1e-7` offset that `process-data.R` adds to every score
- 553 forecasts (0.27%) score exactly zero, and adding the offset the constant parks them 11 log-units below the next smallest value
- No impact: refitting without the offset changed residual skew by 0.01.

### Impact

Both scales now use `tw(link = "log")`, replacing `gaussian(log)` on the log scale and `Gamma(log)` on the natural scale.

Several adjusted estimates moved, particularly the deaths-versus-cases contrast (ratio from 0.17 to 0.38).
All substantive conclusions hold (no model structure differs from the grand mean).

body:
## Problema

O PDF de **Lucro / Prejuízo** (e, na verdade, qualquer relatório gerado em telas estreitas) saía **cortado à direita** — as colunas de valor apareciam truncadas ("R$ 0,…").

## Causa

O gerador de PDF (`PrintButton.tsx`) força o **layout desktop** capturando com `windowWidth ≥ 1024px`, mas usava como **largura de captura** apenas a maior entre a largura visível e a tabela mais larga. Em telas estreitas (celular), essa largura ficava **menor que 1024px**: o conteúdo era disposto em 1024px e recortado para a largura menor — cortando o lado direito.

## Correção

A largura de captura passa a ser a **largura inteira em que o conteúdo foi disposto** (`windowWidth`). Assim o canvas captura tudo que foi renderizado, e o PDF sai completo. Tabelas mais largas que 1024px continuam ampliando `windowWidth` (e a captura acompanha), então nada é perdido.

Mudança de uma linha de lógica, no componente compartilhado por todos os relatórios — beneficia todos os PDFs.

body:
## The leak

Every Hermes attach left a blank tab behind in the one long-lived browser.

`create_session()` asked the control plane for a tab of its own
(`POST …/sessions/<id>/tabs`) and returned the id as `own_tab_id`. The control
plane duly created an `about:blank` target — but Hermes' own `agent-browser`
stack does not connect to it: it selects an existing page. Measured live: a
`browser_navigate` to KSP drove the Example Domain tab the task was already in,
while a fresh `about:blank` target appeared beside it and stayed. One blank tab
per attach, in a browser that never restarts.

## The corrected policy

Attaching creates nothing. A create performs exactly the attach request and
returns exactly the four contract keys; the session reuses the page Hermes
selects anyway. A tab is created **only when an agent or the operator explicitly
asks** through the control plane's authenticated tab routes, and the tab that ask
produces is attributed to the task that asked — same `Target.createTarget` path,
same ownership record, same refusals. Authorized cross-agent access is unchanged.

## What moved

- `provider.py`: `_own_tab` and its constants/validators are **removed**, not
  disabled — no unused compatibility path to drift back into use. `own_tab_id`
  and `own_tab_owner` are gone from the session metadata.
- Tests: `OwnTabTests` is replaced by `AttachCreatesNoTabTests` — exactly one
  request, never the tabs route, exactly four keys, no leftover machinery. The
  fake control plane still answers the tab route as the real one does, so a
  create that asked would be recorded *and* get a usable answer.
- Docs: the provider README, `docs/architecture.md` §Tabs with owners,
  `docs/security-model.md` §55, `infra/README.md`'s route table, the takeover
  runbook, and `tab-service.ts`'s header now state on-demand creation and
  attribution instead of automatic per-task assignment. The runbook's two-agent
  step now requires attaching two tasks to add NO page to the operator's strip.
- `plugin.yaml` 0.2.0 → 0.2.1. **Protocol version unchanged** (`0.1.1`): no wire
  shape moved — create/detach request and response key sets are byte-identical.

Out of scope by design: blocked-tab handoff, cleanup, target affinity, and any
new model tool. Hermes core is untouched.

## Checks (local — GitHub Actions credits are exhausted, no CI run)

- `make test-hermes-provider` — RED first (4 failures, the right ones), then
  GREEN: 61 tests, OK.
- `make check` — build, lint, format:check, typecheck, all package tests, and
  the provider suite: **exit 0**.
- `git diff --check` clean; no binaries; diff reviewed for secrets.
- Nothing outside the worktree was touched: no `~/.hermes`, Docker, Steel,
  Chromium, persistent profile, or other worktrees.

author: yuvaldim
body:
Several problems in this repo cost hours and would have cost minutes with a note. They share a shape: **the symptom appears far from the cause, and the error message names nothing useful.**

`docs/explanation/infrastructure-lessons.md` records them as symptom → cause → how to check.

## What's in it

**Silent failure is the theme.** Four security mechanisms broke without anything turning red — Ed25519 key format (~8 months), signature coverage (since inception), KMS OIDC trust after the repo rename (9 months), and a frontmatter mutation bug. None had a test or scheduled run exercising them. `sign.yml` now runs weekly for exactly that reason.

**OIDC: print the claim, never infer it.** The subject varies by trigger, and `deployment_status` emits an **empty ref** (`repo:owner/name:ref:`) that no branch pattern can match — and which is identical for fork PRs, so a role trusting it is fork-reachable. We guessed wrong three times against an error naming nothing. `Print OIDC Claim` exists to end that.

**SSM/chamber:** everything is a SecureString. Without `--with-decryption` you get a ciphertext, which passes every non-empty check and fails far downstream.

**Neon:** three lookalike identifiers (org id / project name / project id) behind one unhelpful 404; preview-only failures are a branch quota, not your code; and — **measured, contradicting what I'd assumed and repeated** — overriding Preview `DATABASE_URL` does *not* stop branch provisioning. Branch count went 1 → 2 across a single comment-only push. The cleanup workflow is necessary, not a workaround.

**Publishing:** a stale `node_modules` CLI signs with the legacy format and rejects valid dossiers; `lint` exits non-zero on warnings and prints two different clean-output shapes; the registry index is CDN-cached, so `info` is authoritative, not `list`.

**Destructive automation should ship inert and be armed separately** — with the reasoning, since `workflow_dispatch` won't register until a workflow is on the default branch, making "test before merge" impossible.

## Also in this PR

A `head_ref` input for the Neon cleanup workflow. A push to a branch with **no PR** still provisions a Neon branch, and no close event ever fires for it — those orphans had no reclaim path. Found while cleaning up the probe branch from the provisioning test.

`CLAUDE.md` points at the doc, since agents read it first and were among those repeating the mistakes.

author: albardn2
body:
Auditing a week of trips meant opening each one and adding the numbers by hand. The trip list now has a checkbox per row and a **Summary** button that totals the selection.


### What it shows

**Expected Cash**, per currency, with the breakdown asked for — collected, spent on the trip, should return. Cash is never summed across currencies, and a currency that was only *spent* in still gets a row, since that is exactly the case an audit is looking for.

**Net Inventory Change**, per material — loaded, sold, returned, net change, variance. Net change is `returned - loaded`, so it carries losses as well as sales; `sold` is reported beside it because they disagree precisely when stock went missing.

### Where it comes from

`TripDomain.summarize` is built on the `Trip` model's own properties (`expected_cash`, `trip_expenses`, `inventory_reconciliation`) rather than fresh SQL. Those encode which money and which stock actually count — deleted payments, voided invoices, orders soft-deleted before the cascade existed, sale events orphaned by legacy voids. A second implementation in SQL would drift from the per-trip page these totals exist to be checked against. The cash column headers deliberately match that page's *Expected Cash* card, so a total can be reconciled without translating between two vocabularies.

### Three things it says out loud rather than swallowing

Each would otherwise make a total quietly mean less than it appears to:

- **A trip with no end-of-trip stock count has not been counted back in.** It contributes to Sold but not to Net Change, flagged both per row (`*`) and in a banner. Treating its load as an outflow would invent one.
- **Uuids that resolve to nothing** — deleted, or another account's — are listed as missing, not counted as trips that happened to contribute zero.
- **Net change beside sold**, so shrinkage is visible instead of being folded into sales.

### Shape

`GET /trip/summary?trip_uuids=a,b,c`. A GET, and open to everyone who can read a trip, because that is what it is — every figure is already visible on the individual trip pages, this only adds them up. The selection is deduped before summing (the same trip twice must not count twice) and capped at 100 in both the DTO and the UI, so a hundred-trip roll-up cannot become a whole-history scan.

Selection survives paging but is cleared when the filters or tab change, since the rows on screen would no longer explain the number.

### Verification

Against the local database:

- the endpoint's totals **match an independent recomputation** from the per-trip figures — every currency and material, asserted rather than eyeballed;
- the headline cash **matches a hand-written SQL sum** of payments and expenses over the same 20 trips: SYP 5000 collected / 750 spent → 4250, USD 105 / 105 → 0;
- an admin of **another account** asking for these trip uuids gets `trip_count: 0` with every uuid reported missing;
- the same trip twice yields `loaded: 7`, not 14;
- bad input answers 422, not 500 — empty selection, over the cap, unknown query param. `GET /trip/summary` with no params returns 422, proving the static rule is not swallowed by `/<uuid>`;
- driven in the browser end to end: select-all-on-page (20/20, header indeterminate → checked), row clicks that do not navigate, refetch on selection change, Arabic + RTL fully translated, no console errors on a cold load.

18 new tests in `backend/tests/domains/test_trip_summary.py`. `scripts/parity_check.py` still reports **LOST=0**. Frontend `tsc` unchanged at the 70-error baseline; the 12 failing domain tests are the pre-existing transaction/user set.

Notes on what was deliberately left — the end-snapshot convention, the Python-side aggregation cost, and the app not getting this — are in [DEFERRED.md](DEFERRED.md).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


---

## Also in the app (second commit)

Hold a trip in the Expo list → a checkbox column slides in with that trip selected; taps then toggle, and **Summary** opens the same roll-up through the same endpoint.

Laid out for a phone rather than ported: cash as a block per currency (matching the trip detail screen) and stock as a five-column table matching that screen's reconciliation. **Variance moved to its own line** under the row, and only when non-zero — a sixth column squeezed the figures past reading. Cancel or unchecking the last one leaves selection mode; Android back leaves selection rather than the screen; a hint says to hold, since a long press is invisible.

### Fixes made before shipping, each a way the sheet could have shown an untrue number

- **`load()` applied its response unconditionally.** The roll-up walks every stop server-side, closing the sheet doesn't cancel the request (`apiCall` has no abort), and the component stays mounted across a close — so a slow answer for an old selection could land last and paint *its* cash and stock under the new selection's heading, with nothing to correct it. Guarded with a request counter, which also stops a superseded failure from replacing good totals with an error screen, and clears a stale error on success.
- **The currency label was the one text style with no explicit colour**, so it followed the device theme against this sheet's hardcoded white — invisible in dark mode, taking with it which currency a block belongs to (`userInterfaceStyle: automatic` is set).
- **`measure_unit` was interpolated raw**, leaving `kg` English in an Arabic UI when `ENUM_AR` already maps it to `كغ`. Now through `te()`, like the currency.
- **The variance label and its signed number shared one `Text`**, which lets bidi move the sign to the wrong side of the digits under RTL. Split into two.
- **Quantities were formatted to 2 decimals while the endpoint rounds to 3**, so a real `0.001` variance would be flagged non-zero and then printed as `-0`.
- **An earlier padding fix was itself wrong:** it reserved room for a "floating" action bar, but the bar is an in-flow sibling of a shrinking list, so it never overlapped — the padding was ~114px of dead space. Removed; the comment now describes the layout that exists.

### Verification

On the booted simulator against the local API, **in RTL**: both currencies (SYP 5000/750/4250, USD 105/105/0 — matching the hand-written SQL sum above), the variance line with its sign correctly left of the digits, and long material names wrapping instead of truncating. Key parity **426/426** en↔ar, every referenced key resolves, every placeholder supplied by its call site, expo `tsc` unchanged at the **119** baseline.

**One honest gap:** the long-press gesture has no machine coverage — this simulator has no tap automation (`idb` absent, macOS Automation denied) — so selection mode was verified by temporarily seeding the state, screenshotting, and reverting. It needs one human tap. Recorded in [DEFERRED.md](DEFERRED.md) rather than glossed over.

The app's Trips screen is admin-only, so this reaches admins only on mobile.

- Introduce a professional study canvas and replace the large legacy question scratchpad with a shared `StudyCanvasWorkspace` to centralize handwriting/annotation features and enable PDF export and persistence.
- Add interactive educational simulators (functions, molecular and spatial geometry) and improve content/math rendering for didactic pages.
- Move several client data flows from direct Supabase calls to `trpc` for centralized backend access and caching, and add server webhook endpoints for Google Drive callback and Mercado Pago notifications.  

### Description

- Environment and server endpoints: add many new server-only and public env variables in `.env.example` and implement `api/google-drive/callback.ts` and `api/mercadopago/webhook.ts` endpoints hooking into backend services.
- Client branding and i18n: update `client/index.html` (pt-BR meta, favicon, MathJax config) and add `client/public/brand/projeto-vetor-logo.svg` for the new brand.
- Routing & performance: refactor `client/src/App.tsx` to lazy-load many admin/feature pages via `lazyWithRetry`, wrap routes in `Suspense` fallback, normalize legacy `/plataforma/admin` routes, and add many new routes (notebook, simulators, admin batch import, etc.).
- UI & components: update headers/sidebar and dashboard bits (avatar now shows email fallback, sidebar items and feature flags), simplify content renderer imports, and adjust many UI strings to Portuguese.
- Math & formulas: replace inline MathJax/KaTeX setup and improve rendering pipeline; update `MathFormula` to normalize sources and use a queue; update content components to use `display` prop for formulas.
- Persistence & canvas: replace the monolithic `QuestionScratchpad` with a lightweight adapter that mounts the new `StudyCanvasWorkspace`, and add the study-canvas subsystem (`PaperViewport`, `StudyCanvasWorkspace`) including local draft handling, rendering, export and persistence hooks.
- New simulators: add `FunctionSimulator`, `MolecularGeometrySimulator`, and `SpatialGeometrySimulator` components with UIs, rendering and math helpers.
- Data fetching migration: replace direct Supabase calls in `SubscriptionGuard`, `AdminGuard`, `InteractiveQuiz` and other places with `trpc` queries/mutations and local caching strategies, and adapt logic for resolution authors, attempts, reports and access checks.

## Associated issues
Closes https://github.com/cityofaustin/atd-data-tech/issues/25372

Here are the 5 main linter errors we tripped and a little bit I learned about each:

**`react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`**: Calling `setState` inside `useEffect` (ex: syncing props to state) causes an extra render after paint. We should prefer deriving state, adjusting during render, or event handlers. ([more info](https://react.dev/learn/you-might-not-need-an-effect))

**`react-hooks/immutability`**: Mutating props, state, or other values that React treats as snapshots (ex: `obj.field = x` then `setState(obj)`). Updates should create new objects/arrays. ([more info](https://react.dev/reference/rules/components-and-hooks-must-be-pure))

**`react-hooks/purity`**: Impure work during render (`Date.now()`, `Math.random()`, etc.). Render should be a pure function of props/state so Strict Mode / Compiler can safely re-run it. ([more info](https://react.dev/reference/rules/components-and-hooks-must-be-pure))

**`react-hooks/preserve-manual-memoization`**: Your `useMemo` / `useCallback` dependency list doesn’t match what the Compiler infers (ex: dependency array list `user?.email` but the callback closes over `user`). body:
The composition section of the data-export page was written against the legacy Composition API. Verified the current behaviour against `atticus-backend@dev` (`a6f6950`) and `atticus-frontend`.

## Why

`GET /fhir/r5/Composition/{id}` (`report_server/api/fhir_r5/endpoints/Composition.py`) parses the id as a legacy `report_id` and builds sections from `BlockORM` rows. Capture-API reports store answers in `report.response_items` and never write blocks, so the endpoint returns a Composition with an empty `section[]` — or an unrelated document when the id collides with a real report. Removal is tracked in Tiro-health/atticus-backend#3388.

## The modern flow

On submit (`apps/subjects/src/pages/EditReport/action.ts`):

1. `PUT /QuestionnaireResponse/{id}` → `status: completed`
2. `POST /QuestionnaireResponse/{id}/$extract` — persists the extracted resources into `extracted_resource` plus an `ExtractionProvenance`
3. `POST /Task/{id}/$complete` — links them as `composition` outputs

Retrieval is `GET /Task?_id=…&_include=Task:output:Composition` (or `Task:output` for everything). This is the only read path: the catchall `ExtractedResource` router exposes just `POST`/`DELETE`, and `/Provenance` has no `GET`.

## Shape corrections

Checked against the generated blueprint (`sdc/composition/strategies/v1.py`, `models/api/fhir_r5/CompositionTemplate.py`):

| Documented | Actual |
| --- | --- |
| id == report id | independent `extracted_resource` id |
| `status: preliminary` | `status: final` |
| type `11506-3` "Report" | template's coding, else `11506-3` *Progress note* |
| sections carry a fixed LOINC/SNOMED `code` | no `section.code` is emitted |
| `subject`, `author`, `date` present | absent unless the blueprint pins them |
| no server-side PDF/HTML export | `POST /Composition/$render?format=pdf\|html` exists on the sdc_server |

Still accurate and left as-is: the `response` + `task` redirect params, and single-language collapsing (`filter_composition_by_language` drops sections lacking the QR's language).

## Changes

- `api/data-export` — rewrote "Fetch the Composition" around `GET /Task` + `_include`, corrected the example Bundle, added a deprecation note for `GET /Composition/{id}`, replaced the section-code mapping advice, fixed the PDF claim
- `fhir/Task` — added the missing `composition` row to the output-types table (the code is `composition` for every extracted resource, including Observations)

`npm run build` passes.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The Task reference page documents no `_include` parameters at all, though the server supports eight (`Task.py:526`).

author: marinrzv
body:
## Problem

With `simulation.enabled: true` the simulated user keeps talking after the agent has delivered its diagnosis ("thanks, I'll get an admin to grant that"). The agent's **final** turn is then a one-line acknowledgement — "Will do.", "You're welcome." — while the real diagnosis sits two turns back.

An `llm_judge` criterion that sets `include_agent_output: true` **without** `include_dialog: true` receives only that final turn. The judge sees no diagnosis and scores `0.00`, so a fully correct investigation fails the task.

Six troubleshoot tasks failed exactly this way in the 2026-07-28 nightly, each with a correct root cause in turn 1.

## Change

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `scripts/check-judge-dialog.py` | Flags `llm_judge` criteria that grade the last turn only. Accepts task YAML paths or a directory. |
| `.github/workflows/judge-dialog-gate.yml` | Runs the check on `pull_request` (and `workflow_dispatch`), scoped to the troubleshoot task YAMLs the PR adds or modifies. |

A task is reported when **all** of these hold:

1. `simulation.enabled` is `true` — multi-turn, so a last-turn-only grade can miss the diagnosis. Single-turn tasks are fine; their last turn *is* the answer.
2. It has an `llm_judge` criterion with `include_agent_output: true`.
3. That criterion does not set `include_dialog: true`.

Failures are emitted as `::error file=…,line=…` annotations, so they render inline on the PR diff at the offending `- type: llm_judge` line.

## Scoping

The gate checks only the task YAMLs a PR **adds or modifies** (`--diff-filter=AM`), so the ~194 existing tasks that predate this rule are not retroactively blocked. `workflow_dispatch` scans the whole skill directory instead, for a full sweep on demand.

There is no `paths:` filter on the workflow, so it can be wired as a required check — it exits 0 when a PR touches no troubleshoot task YAMLs. To cover other skills later, widen the pathspec in the "Collect changed task YAMLs" step.

## Verification

Run locally (`pip install pyyaml`):

```bash
# current main — every task still grades the last turn only
python3 scripts/check-judge-dialog.py tests/tasks/uipath-troubleshoot
# FAIL - 194 llm_judge criteria grade the last turn only:   (exit 1)

# a task fixed by #2293
python3 scripts/check-judge-dialog.py <fixed-task.yaml>
# OK - every simulated task's llm_judge grades the full dialog.   (exit 0)

# no paths (PR touches no tasks)
python3 scripts/check-judge-dialog.py
# OK - ...   (exit 0)
```

All three paths confirmed, plus the singular-grammar branch (`1 llm_judge criterion grades`).

## Relationship to #2293

Split out of #2293, which now carries only the task-YAML fixes (`include_dialog: true` on 194 tasks + the `CLAUDE.md` judge template). The two can merge in either order — because the gate is scoped to changed files, merging this first does not retroactively fail anything.
